claims.text: OER activity in epitaxial high-entropy perovskite oxides is governed by cooperative redox dynamics among multiple transition-metal cations.
Operational durability is governed by cooperative redox dynamics among multiple transition-metal cations.
Atomic-scale mixing promotes d-orbital coupling among the different transition-metal cations.
The multication electronic interaction optimizes the distribution of adsorption energies for oxygenated OER intermediates.
Intimate multication mixing enables simultaneous oxidation and reduction events across neighboring cations.
Cooperative cation redox changes fine-tune the binding strengths of OER intermediates.
The proposed cooperative redox mechanism facilitates faster electron transfer.
The proposed cooperative redox mechanism improves desorption of OER intermediates.
A physical mixture of single-B-site perovskites lacks a contiguous multication lattice and therefore lacks effective inter-cation orbital coupling.
The proposed high-entropy catalyst is the epitaxial perovskite LaCr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2O3–δ.
Relative to a physical mixture of single-B-site perovskites, the epitaxial high-entropy catalyst will have higher current density at a fixed overpotential.
Relative to the physical-mixture baseline, the epitaxial high-entropy catalyst will have a higher turnover frequency.
Relative to the physical-mixture baseline, the epitaxial high-entropy catalyst will exhibit less performance decay over 120 hours.
Operando XPS will show dynamic oxidation-state shifts across several cations in the high-entropy film.
Cooperative oxidation-state shifts will be diminished or absent in the physical mixture.
The controlled comparison will match morphology, surface area, particle size, and active-facet exposure between the high-entropy material and physical mixture.
The hypothesis is scoped to alkaline aqueous OER at pH 13, approximately 25 °C, and approximately 320 mV overpotential.
The proposed mechanism may not extend to substantially different catalyst morphologies or reaction conditions.
